docs.title: HCBench
docs.text: HCBench standardizes single-cell CNA caller outputs and evaluates them against simulated ground truth or against other callers.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Use Python 3.10 or newer:

pip install git+https://github.com/compbioclub/HCBench.git@main

Installation includes NumPy, pandas (>=2.0,<3), SciPy, scikit-learn, and Biopython. Install the extras needed for your inputs or analysis:

# Read Alleloscope RDS files
pip install "hcbench[rds] @ git+https://github.com/compbioclub/HCBench.git@main"
# Run focal gene and pathway enrichment
pip install "hcbench[enrichment] @ git+https://github.com/compbioclub/HCBench.git@main"

VCF conversion needs BCFtools, and CNA phylogeny needs Lazac. Install them separately and put the required executable on PATH.

docs.title: Prepare your inputs
docs.text:
Choose the workflow for your data:

  • Parsers: convert CHISEL, Alleloscope, CNRein, SEACON, or SIGNALS outputs into CNA matrices.
  • HCBench-sim: compare caller matrices with matching HCDSIM ground truth.
  • HCBench-real: compare at least two callers for the same sample; no ground truth is required.

A standardized CNA CSV has region as its first column and cell identifiers as the remaining columns. Combined values use hap1|hap2 (for example, 2|1); split haplotype matrices contain numeric values. Keep caller names and input paths in the same order. Clone comparisons also need clusters.csv with cell_id and clone_id; read-depth and VAF analyses need their corresponding sequencing inputs.

docs.title: Initialize and run
docs.text:
bin_size and genome are required when creating a CNA parser, GTBench, or RealBench:

  • bin_size: a positive integer in base pairs, such as 100000 for 100 kb. Use the resolution of your CNA data.
  • genome: "hg19" or "hg38", matching your input coordinates.

Methods use this configuration. Initialization prints:

Bin size: 100000 bp
Genome: hg38

The following example compares two already standardized CNA files. Replace the paths and configuration with those for your sample:

from hcbench.realbench import RealBench

bench = RealBench(bin_size=100000, genome="hg38", output_dir="output/realbench")
bench.cna_values(
    tool_cna_files=[
        "results/Alleloscope/haplotype_combined.csv",
        "results/CHISEL/haplotype_combined.csv",
    ],
    tool_names=["Alleloscope", "CHISEL"],
    outfile_prefix="cna_values",
)

This writes cna_values_rmse.csv, cna_values_scc.csv, and cna_values_acc.csv under output/realbench/. Each file is a caller-by-caller comparison matrix. See the workflow tutorials above for parsing, ground-truth evaluation, and other methods.

docs.title: Choose an event-analysis resolution
docs.text:
With the default event-size thresholds, analysis is available for:

CNA bin_size Event categories <= 3,000,000 bp focal, medium, broad > 3,000,000 and <= 10,000,000 bp medium, broad > 10,000,000 bp broad

Event length is End - Start + 1: focal is below 3 Mb, medium is from 3 Mb through 10 Mb, and broad is above 10 Mb. Whole-chromosome and whole-genome events are reported as broad. Categories unavailable at your resolution have no annotation or category-metric rows; a missing comparison is reported as NA rather than evidence of no events.

RealBench.focal_genes_and_pathways() requires bin_size <= 3,000,000. At coarser resolutions it prints a skip message, returns None, and creates no new enrichment results. For supported resolutions, see the focal gene and pathway tutorial.

docs.title: HCBench-sim
docs.text: HCBench-sim evaluates inferred hcCNA profiles against the hcCNA-bench GT. The evaluation is organized around five evaluation questions: CNA detection, clone detection, evolution tracking, accumulated complex hcCNA detection, and CN phasing.

docs.title: Prepare inputs and initialize
docs.text:
Prepare standardized caller CNA matrices and matching HCDSIM ground truth. Combined files use a first region column and one column per cell; split files contain one haplotype or allele per matrix. Clone files need cell_id and clone_id. Evolution-onset methods also need the corresponding GT change tables; stability analysis needs a Newick tree.

Keep caller paths and tool_names in the same order. Use cell-level files together or clone-level files together. Replace all /path/to/ paths below with your data. Run the setup block once before the method examples.

bin_size and genome are required when creating a CNA parser, GTBench, or RealBench:

  • bin_size: a positive integer in base pairs, such as 100000 for 100 kb. Use the resolution of your CNA data.
  • genome: "hg19" or "hg38", matching your input coordinates.

Methods use this configuration. Initialization prints:

Bin size: 100000 bp
Genome: hg38

With the default event-size thresholds, analysis is available for:

CNA bin_size Event categories <= 3,000,000 bp focal, medium, broad > 3,000,000 and <= 10,000,000 bp medium, broad > 10,000,000 bp broad

Event length is End - Start + 1: focal is below 3 Mb, medium is from 3 Mb through 10 Mb, and broad is above 10 Mb. Whole-chromosome and whole-genome events are reported as broad. Categories unavailable at your resolution have no annotation or category-metric rows; a missing comparison is reported as NA rather than evidence of no events.

For evolution-onset analyses, supply change tables containing only the event categories appropriate for your resolution. Those methods read the change tables you provide. Phylogeny examples require lazac on PATH.

from hcbench.gtbench import GTBench

# All benchmark outputs will be written under this directory
bench = GTBench(output_dir="/path/to/results/gt_output/cell_level", bin_size=100000, genome="hg38")

All files are saved under bench.output_dir. Methods with outfile use that filename; phasing uses {outprefix}_{mode}.csv. cna_values() returns its metrics DataFrame as well as saving the CSV. Methods that only save files, including complex_hccnas() and unique-profile counts/sizes, return None.

docs.title: CNA Detection
docs.text: This section evaluates the accuracy of allele-specific copy number alterations (acCNAs) and haplotype-specific copy number alterations (hcCNAs) at the value and state levels.

docs.title: acCNA values
docs.text:
Are allele-, cell/clone-, and locus-specific CN values correct?

Assesses quantitative accuracy using RMSE and SCC for major and minor alleles. It also uses ACC to measure the percentage of loci where the full allele-specific string is exactly correct.

# acCNA values
bench.cna_values(
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/signals/minor_major.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/minor_major.csv",
    ],
    cna_profile_file="/path/to/gt/cell/minor_major.csv",
    tool_names=[
        "signals",
        "seacon",
    ],
    haplotype="combined",
    outfile="cna_values_accna.csv",
)

docs.title: acCNA states
docs.text:
Are allele-, cell/clone-, and locus-specific CN loss, gain, and neutral states correct?

Treats copy number detection as a binary classification problem (Gain, Neutral, Loss). Performance is measured via a suite of statistical metrics (AUROC, Sensitivity, F1-Score, etc.) to determine the reliability of calling specific genomic states.

# acCNA states
bench.cna_states(
    tool_hap1_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/signals/minor.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/minor.csv",
    ],
    tool_hap2_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/signals/major.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/major.csv",
    ],
    tool_names=[
        "signals",
        "seacon",
    ],
    profile_hap1_cna_file="/path/to/gt/cell/minor.csv",
    profile_hap2_cna_file="/path/to/gt/cell/major.csv",
    type="acCNA",
    outfile="cna_states_accna.csv",
)

docs.title: hcCNA values
docs.text:
Are haplotype-, cell/clone-, and locus-specific CN values correct?

Calculates the average RMSE and SCC across both individual haplotypes and evaluates the rate of exact matches for the phased CN strings (ACC).

# hcCNA values
bench.cna_values(
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/signals/haplotype_combined.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_combined.csv",
    ],
    cna_profile_file="/path/to/gt/cell/haplotype_combined.csv",
    tool_names=[
        "signals",
        "seacon",
    ],
    haplotype="combined",
    outfile="cna_values_hccna.csv",
)

docs.title: hcCNA states
docs.text:
Are haplotype-, cell/clone-, and locus-specific CN loss, gain, and neutral states correct?

Assesses phased CN calling performance via binary classification across multiple states (Gain/Loss/Neutral), providing a comprehensive statistical breakdown of detection sensitivity and specificity.

# hcCNA states
bench.cna_states(
    tool_hap1_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/signals/haplotype_1.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_1.csv",
    ],
    tool_hap2_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/signals/haplotype_2.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_2.csv",
    ],
    tool_names=[
        "signals",
        "seacon",
    ],
    profile_hap1_cna_file="/path/to/gt/cell/haplotype_1.csv",
    profile_hap2_cna_file="/path/to/gt/cell/haplotype_2.csv",
    type="hcCNA",
    outfile="cna_states_hccna.csv",
)

docs.title: Clone Detection
docs.text: This section evaluates the accuracy of inferring clonal architecture and the diversity of unique CN profiles within a tumor population.

docs.title: Global tumor clones
docs.text:
Are global tumor clones correct?

Uses global metrics like Adjusted Mutual Information (AMI) and Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) to compare predicted labels against the ground truth. This provides a high-level assessment of how well the overall population structure is captured.

# Global tumor clones
bench.global_tumor_clones(
    tool_clone_files=[
        "/path/to/signals/clusters.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/clusters.csv",
    ],
    tool_names=[
        "signals",
        "seacon",
    ],
)

docs.title: Rare and dominant clones
docs.text:
Are rare and dominant clones correct?

Evaluates clustering accuracy stratified by clone size using Clone Size Deviation (CSD). It measures whether specific clones (regardless of size) are being merged into larger clusters (positive deviation) or "shattered" into many small groups (negative deviation).

First, generate the GT clusters.csv from HCDSIM's profile/barcodes.txt. The barcode file has no header and contains one cell ID per line. In HCDSIM cell IDs, the prefix before the first underscore identifies the clone; for example, clone1_cell1 belongs to clone1.

from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv(
    "/path/to/HCDSIM/profile/barcodes.txt",
    sep="\t",
    comment=None,
    index_col=False,
    header=None,
    names=["cell_id"],
)
df["clone_id"] = df["cell_id"].str.split("_", n=1).str[0]

gt_cluster_file = Path("results/gt/clusters.csv")
gt_cluster_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
df.to_csv(gt_cluster_file, index=False)

This writes a CSV with cell_id and clone_id columns. Keep the full cell IDs so they match those in the caller cluster files. Use the generated GT file with the bench initialized above:

# Rare and dominant clones
bench.rare_and_dominant_clones(
    tool_cluster_files=[
        "/path/to/signals/clusters.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/clusters.csv",
    ],
    gt_cluster_file=str(gt_cluster_file),
    tool_names=[
        "signals",
        "seacon",
    ],
    outfile="rare_and_dominant_clones.csv",
)

docs.title: Unique acCNA profiles
docs.text:
Are unique allele- and cell-specific CN profiles correct?

Analyzes "Unique Profile Groups" (UPGs) using Unique Profile Count Error (UPCE) and Unique Profile Size Deviation (UPSD). These metrics detect if distinct biological profiles are being over-smoothed (merged) or over-fragmented due to noise.

# Unique acCNA profiles
bench.unique_cna_profile_counts(
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/gt/cell/minor_major.csv",
        "/path/to/signals/minor_major.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/minor_major.csv",
    ],
    tool_names=[
        "GT",
        "signals",
        "seacon",
    ],
    outfile="unique_cna_profile_counts_accna.csv",
)

bench.unique_cna_profile_sizes(
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/signals/minor_major.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/minor_major.csv",
    ],
    gt_cna_file="/path/to/gt/cell/minor_major.csv",
    tool_names=[
        "signals",
        "seacon",
    ],
    outfile="unique_cna_profile_sizes_accna.csv",
)

docs.title: Unique hcCNA profiles
docs.text:
Are unique haplotype- and cell-specific CN profiles correct?

Quantifies performance based on cells sharing identical haplotype-specific CN strings across the genome using UPCE and UPSD metrics.

# Unique hcCNA profiles
bench.unique_cna_profile_counts(
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/gt/cell/haplotype_combined.csv",
        "/path/to/signals/haplotype_combined.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_combined.csv",
    ],
    tool_names=[
        "GT",
        "signals",
        "seacon",
    ],
    outfile="unique_cna_profile_counts_hccna.csv",  # Output CSV name under output_dir
)

bench.unique_cna_profile_sizes(
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/signals/haplotype_combined.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_combined.csv",
    ],
    gt_cna_file="/path/to/gt/cell/haplotype_combined.csv",
    tool_names=[
        "signals",
        "seacon",
    ],
    outfile="unique_cna_profile_sizes_hccna.csv",
)

docs.title: Evolution Tracking
docs.text: This section evaluates whether inferred CN phylogenies and complex hcCNA evolutionary events agree with the ground truth.

docs.title: acCNA phylogeny
docs.text:
Are allele- and cell-specific CN phylogenies correct?

Calculates a parsimony score for each supplied CN profile. Include GT in the input list to compare its score with caller scores.

# acCNA phylogeny
bench.cna_phylogeny(
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/gt/cell/minor_major.csv",
        "/path/to/signals/minor_major.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/minor_major.csv",
    ],
    tool_names=[
        "GT",
        "signals",
        "seacon",
    ],
    outfile="cna_phylogeny_accna.csv",
)

docs.title: hcCNA phylogeny
docs.text:
Are haplotype- and cell-specific CN phylogenies correct?

Calculates parsimony scores from phased CN profiles. The output lists each tool and its Parsimony score.

# hcCNA phylogeny
bench.cna_phylogeny(
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/gt/cell/haplotype_combined.csv",
        "/path/to/signals/haplotype_combined.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_combined.csv",
    ],
    tool_names=[
        "GT",
        "signals",
        "seacon",
    ],
    outfile="cna_phylogeny_hccna.csv",
)

docs.title: Prepare size-specific change tables
docs.text:
Before running the four onset and stability analyses below, split the HCDSIM cell_changes.csv and clone_changes.csv tables by event size. Use Length in base pairs: focal is below 3,000,000 bp, medium is from 3,000,000 through 10,000,000 bp, and broad is above 10,000,000 bp. Keep the other change-table columns for the benchmark methods.

The following example reads both files from your HCDSIM profile directory and saves one CSV per size present in each table. Replace the input directory with yours. Missing or nonnumeric lengths must be corrected before classification.

from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

profile_dir = Path("/path/to/HCDSIM/profile")
changes_by_level = {}

for level in ("cell", "clone"):
    df = pd.read_csv(profile_dir / f"{level}_changes.csv")
    df["Length"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Length"], errors="coerce")
    if df["Length"].isna().any():
        raise ValueError(f"Correct missing or nonnumeric Length values in {level}_changes.csv")

    df["size"] = np.select(
        [
            df["Length"] < 3_000_000,
            (df["Length"] >= 3_000_000) & (df["Length"] <= 10_000_000),
        ],
        ["focal", "medium"],
        default="broad",
    )

    output_dir = Path("results/gt") / f"{level}-level"
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    changes_by_level[level] = {}
    if level == "cell":
        df.rename(columns = {
            "Clone": "Parent",
            "Cell": "Child"
        }, inplace=True)

    for size in df["size"].unique():
        out_file = output_dir / f"{level}_changes_split_annotated_{size}.csv"
        df.loc[df["size"] == size].to_csv(out_file, index=False)
        changes_by_level[level][size] = out_file

Cell-level files are saved under results/gt/cell-level/ with names such as cell_changes_split_annotated_focal.csv; clone-level files are saved under results/gt/clone-level/ with names such as clone_changes_split_annotated_focal.csv. Categories absent from an input table produce no file.

The examples below use the cell-level files. For clone-level analysis, select changes_by_level["clone"] and supply matching clone-level haplotype matrices. For stability analysis, the tree node names must match the parent and child identifiers in the chosen change table. These methods evaluate the supplied change file; use one size-specific file per call.

docs.title: Parental CN at onset
docs.text: Are parent CNs of complex hcCNAs correct at onset? Assesses whether the model correctly identifies the pre-event (parental) copy number state at the exact moment an alteration arises during evolution, using metrics like ACC and RMSE.

docs.title: CN change at onset
docs.text: Are CN changes of complex hcCNAs correct at onset? Evaluates the model's accuracy in capturing the magnitude and direction of the copy number transition (e.g., a gain from 1 to 3) from parent to child.

docs.title: Complex hcCNA at onset
docs.text: Are complex hcCNAs correct at onset? A holistic measure requiring the parent state, child state, and the resulting change to all match the ground truth. This reflects the end-to-end reliability in pinpointing true evolutionary transitions.

docs.title: Complex hcCNA stability
docs.text:
Are complex hcCNAs stable throughout evolution? Evaluates whether a detected alteration is correctly tracked as a stable, heritable state across all descendant clones following its initial onset.

Run the preparation step above first. This loop evaluates only sizes that have a change file and are supported by bench.bin_size: all three sizes up to 3 Mb, medium/broad above 3 Mb through 10 Mb, and broad above 10 Mb.

# Run after preparing the size-specific change tables above
# Parental CN at onset: parental_cn_at_onset
# CN change at onset: cn_change_at_onset
# Complex hcCNA at onset: complex_hccna_at_onset
# Complex hcCNA stability: complex_hccna_stability
change_files = changes_by_level["cell"]
event_sizes = ["broad"]
if bench.bin_size <= 10_000_000:
    event_sizes.insert(0, "medium")
if bench.bin_size <= 3_000_000:
    event_sizes.insert(0, "focal")
event_sizes = [size for size in event_sizes if size in change_files]
for size in event_sizes:

    bench.parental_cn_at_onset(
        tool_hap1_cna_files=[
            "/path/to/signals/haplotype_1.csv",
            "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_1.csv",
        ],
        tool_hap2_cna_files=[
            "/path/to/signals/haplotype_2.csv",
            "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_2.csv",
        ],
        tool_names=[
            "signals",
            "seacon",
        ],
        changes_file=str(change_files[size]),
        outfile=f"parental_cn_at_onset_{size}.csv",
    )

    bench.cn_change_at_onset(
        tool_hap1_cna_files=[
            "/path/to/signals/haplotype_1.csv",
            "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_1.csv",
        ],
        tool_hap2_cna_files=[
            "/path/to/signals/haplotype_2.csv",
            "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_2.csv",
        ],
        tool_names=[
            "signals",
            "seacon",
        ],
        changes_file=str(change_files[size]),
        outfile=f"cn_change_at_onset_{size}.csv",
    )

    bench.complex_hccna_at_onset(
        tool_hap1_cna_files=[
            "/path/to/signals/haplotype_1.csv",
            "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_1.csv",
        ],
        tool_hap2_cna_files=[
            "/path/to/signals/haplotype_2.csv",
            "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_2.csv",
        ],
        tool_names=[
            "signals",
            "seacon",
        ],
        changes_file=str(change_files[size]),
        outfile=f"complex_hccna_at_onset_{size}.csv",
    )

    bench.complex_hccna_stability(
        tool_hap1_cna_files=[
            "/path/to/signals/haplotype_1.csv",
            "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_1.csv",
        ],
        tool_hap2_cna_files=[
            "/path/to/signals/haplotype_2.csv",
            "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_2.csv",
        ],
        tool_names=[
            "signals",
            "seacon",
        ],
        changes_file=str(change_files[size]),
        tree_file="/path/to/tree/tree_new.newick",
        outfile=f"complex_hccna_stability_{size}.csv",
    )

docs.title: Accumulated Complex hcCNA Detection
docs.text: This section assesses the final "burden" of complex hcCNAs. Rather than looking at the moment of onset, it evaluates the final segmented copy number states observed in terminal clones or cells across focal, medium, and broad scales.

docs.title: Complex hcCNAs
docs.text:
Are accumulated complex hcCNAs correct?

Compares predicted complex hcCNA profiles against the ground truth (GT) using RMSE, SCC, and ACC to assess numerical agreement and exact matches of haplotype-specific CN values.

Use the bench initialized above. Supply either a combined GT CNA matrix through gt_cna_file, or an existing GT annotation DataFrame through gt_annotated_df. Keep tool_cna_files and tool_names in the same order.

docs.title: Evaluate from a GT CNA matrix
docs.text:
When you have a combined GT matrix, complex_hccnas() annotates it before comparing the caller profiles:

bench.complex_hccnas(
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/signals/haplotype_combined.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_combined.csv",
    ],
    gt_cna_file="/path/to/gt/cell/haplotype_combined.csv",
    tool_names=["signals", "seacon"],
    threshold=0.8,
    outprefix="complex_hccnas_",
)

The default threshold=0.8 controls whole-chromosome/genome event annotation. Use chromosomes=["chr1", "chr2"] to restrict GT annotation and caller profiles to selected chromosomes.

docs.title: Evaluate with existing GT annotations
docs.text:
If you already have a GT annotation CSV, load it with pandas and pass the resulting DataFrame as gt_annotated_df. Set gt_cna_file=None; this argument must still be supplied. The method uses the supplied event labels directly, so threshold does not change them.

The table needs cell, value, size, and type, plus either region or all three coordinate columns Chrom, Start, and End. Values use haplotype pairs such as 2|1; size labels are focal, medium, or broad. Each row describes a cell and an input CNA region, with cell IDs and region coordinates matching the caller matrices at the configured bin resolution. A Segment column alone cannot replace these region coordinates.

To create a suitable CSV from a combined GT matrix, save annotations with detect_cnv_type=True:

from pathlib import Path
from hcbench.parsers.gt import GTParser

Path("results/gt").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
gt_parser = GTParser(
    input_path="/path/to/gt/cell/haplotype_combined.csv",
    output_path="results/gt",
    bin_size=bench.bin_size,
    genome=bench.genome,
)
gt_parser.annotate_segments(
    "/path/to/gt/cell/haplotype_combined.csv",
    threshold=0.8,
    detect_cnv_type=True,
    out_file="ground_truth_classified.csv",
)

This writes results/gt/ground_truth_classified.csv. GTParser.annotate_segments() returns None, so load the saved CSV for evaluation:

import pandas as pd

gt_annotated_df = pd.read_csv(
    "results/gt/ground_truth_classified.csv",
    dtype={"cell": str, "Chrom": str, "value": str},
)
bench.complex_hccnas(
    gt_cna_file=None,
    gt_annotated_df=gt_annotated_df,
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/signals/haplotype_combined.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_combined.csv",
    ],
    tool_names=["signals", "seacon"],
    outprefix="complex_hccnas_",
)

When supplying gt_annotated_df together with chromosomes, prepare the DataFrame with only those chromosomes; the method applies chromosomes to the caller profiles but does not filter the supplied GT table by chromosome.

Both input options write {outprefix}metrics.csv under bench.output_dir and return None. With the examples above, the filename is complex_hccnas_metrics.csv. Rows report Size, Type, ACC, SCC, RMSE, and Tool. Event categories excluded by bench.bin_size have no metric rows; comparisons without matching cell/region entries have missing metrics.

docs.title: Mirrored-subclonal-CNAs
docs.text:
Are accumulated Mirrored-Subclonal-CNAs correct? Specifically evaluates Mirrored-Subclonal events—patterns where different subclones have reciprocal alterations—at the clone level to determine if these complex evolutionary outcomes are accurately reconstructed.

# Mirrored-subclonal-CNAs
bench.mirrored_subclonal_cnas(
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/signals/haplotype_combined.csv",
        "/path/to/seacon/haplotype_combined.csv",
    ],
    tool_names=[
        "signals",
        "seacon",
    ],
    changes_file= "/path/to/gt/mirrored_subclonal_cnas_cnas.csv"
)

docs.title: CN Phasing
docs.text: This section evaluates the accuracy of haplotype-specific phasing, determining how effectively a model assigns copy number states to the correct parental haplotype (e.g., distinguishing a 2|1 state from 1|2).

docs.title: Global CN phasing
docs.text:
Are CN values correctly phased? Measures the mismatch error between predicted and ground-truth phase strings. Evaluation is performed in two modes:

  • GT-heterozygous mode: Reflects combined errors in both phasing and the ability to retain heterozygous loci.
  • Shared-heterozygous mode: Isolates the phasing accuracy specifically at loci where both the prediction and ground truth agree the site is informative (heterozygous).

The analysis uses normalized Hamming distance to account for potential global phase flips.

# Shared-heterozygous mode
bench.global_cn_phasing(

This function evaluates clone-size consistency at the cell profile level. It first derives clone sizes from the GT CNA matrix (cells sharing identical bin-level CNA profiles are grouped as one profile-clone), then compares each tool's inferred profile-clone sizes against GT.

The function writes:

  • a detailed per-cell comparison table
  • a mean summary grouped by GT cluster_size

docs.title: Parameters

docs.text:

  • rows: genomic regions (first column as index when reading)
  • columns: cell IDs
  • values: CNA states (e.g., "1|1")

region,cell_001,cell_002,cell_003
chr1:1-100000,1|1,1|1,2|1
chr1:100001-200000,1|1,1|1,2|1

  • for tool matrices, all-empty columns are dropped before processing

  2. os.path.join(self.output_dir, f"mean_{outfile}")

global_tumor_clones(
    tool_clone_files: List[str],
    tool_names: List[str],
) -> pd.DataFrame

For each tool, the function loads clusters.csvfile and calculates:

  • ARI: Adjusted Rand Index between cell_id and clone_id
  • AMI: Adjusted Mutual Information between cell_id and clone_id

It aggregates results across tools into a single table, writes it to:

  • {self.output_dir}/global_tumor_clones.csv

and returns the result as a DataFrame.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description tool_clone_files List[str] List of file paths, one per tool. Each file should be a CSV containing at least cell_id and clone_id columns. tool_names List[str] List of tool names aligned with tool_clone_files (same length and order).

docs.title: Input File Format
docs.text:
Each tool_clone_files[i] is expected to be a CSV with at least:

  • cell_id: string cell identifier, expected format like "<cluster>_<rest>" so that cell_id.split("_")[0] yields the reference cluster label
  • clone_id: clone assignment label from the tool

Example:

cell_id,clone_id
A_cell0001,1
A_cell0002,1
B_cell0003,2

From this, the function derives:

  • clusters1 = ["A", "A", "B"]
  • clusters2 = ["1", "1", "2"]

docs.title: Return Type
docs.text: • pd.DataFrame

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
A DataFrame with one row per tool:

Column Meaning Tool Tool name from tool_names ARI Adjusted Rand Index between derived clusters and clone_id AMI Adjusted Mutual Information between derived clusters and clone_id

docs.title: Output
docs.text: • Writes a CSV summary to: os.path.join(self.output_dir, "global_tumor_clones.csv")

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from hcbench.gtbench import gtbench

# Suppose self.output_dir = "out/gt_output"

gtbench_runner = gtbench.GTBench(
    output_dir=f"out/gt_output/", bin_size=100000 , genome="hg38")

tool_clone_files = [
    "out/chisel/clusters.csv",
    "out/alleloscope/clusters.csv",
    "out/signals/clusters.csv",
]
tool_names = ["CHISEL", "Alleloscope", "SIGNALS"]

# Call from within your class instance that has self.output_dir (out/gt_output/) defined
df = gtbench_runner.global_tumor_clones(
    tool_clone_files=tool_clone_files,
    tool_names=tool_names,
)

print(df)
# Expected output (values are illustrative):
#           Tool     ARI     AMI
# 0       CHISEL  0.230   0.301
# 1  Alleloscope  0.5321  0.4880
# 2      SIGNALS  0.8123  0.7451

After running, you will also find:

out/gt_output/global_tumor_clones.csv

containing the same summary table.

docs.text:
cna_states(
    self,
    tool_hap1_cna_files: List[str],
    tool_hap2_cna_files: List[str],
    tool_names: List[str],
    profile_hap1_cna_file: str,
    profile_hap2_cna_file: str,
    type: str = "hcCNA",

    outfile: str = "cna_states.csv",
) -> pd.DataFrame

This function performs CNA class–specific evaluation by stratifying genomic bins into predefined CNA categories (e.g., gain/neutral/loss, exact CN states) and then computing clone-level metrics for each category, haplotype, and tool.

It supports both:

  • hcCNA: haplotype-specific copy numbers (hap1, hap2)
  • acCNA: allele-specific copy numbers (minor, major)

For each tool, the function:

  1. Loads GT haplotype CNA profiles (hap1/hap2 or minor/major).
  2. Loads tool predictions for hap1 and hap2.
  3. Re-bins regions to a uniform resolution (self.bin_size) and aligns GT vs predictions.
  4. For each CNA category (condition), saves category-specific bin tables into an output folder.
  5. Computes clone-level metrics within each category and aggregates results into one summary table.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description tool_hap1_cna_files List[str] List of tool prediction CSVs for haplotype 1 (or minor allele if type="acCNA"). Must align with tool_names. tool_hap2_cna_files List[str] List of tool prediction CSVs for haplotype 2 (or major allele if type="acCNA"). Must align with tool_names. tool_names List[str] Tool names used to create output directories and label result rows. profile_hap1_cna_file str Path to GT CNA profile CSV for haplotype 1 (or minor). profile_hap2_cna_file str Path to GT CNA profile CSV for haplotype 2 (or major). type str CNA type. Must be "hcCNA" or "acCNA". Default: "hcCNA". outfile str Output filename for the final aggregated result table. Default: "cna_states.csv".

docs.title: GT files: profile_hap1_cna_file, profile_hap2_cna_file
docs.text:
Expected to be CNA matrices with:

  • one column named region
  • remaining columns as cell IDs
  • values as integer CNA states or strings convertible to numeric (depends on your pipeline)

Loaded via read_and_drop_empty(...) and then indexed by "region".

docs.title: Tool prediction files: tool_hap1_cna_files, tool_hap2_cna_files
docs.text:
Expected to be CSVs with:

  • region column
  • cell columns

Processing:

  • tool predictions are loaded with pd.read_csv(...).fillna(-1)
  • regions are re-binned using:
split_all_regions(df.set_index("region"), self.bin_size)
  • GT and predictions are aligned by:
gt_h1, p_h1 = align(gt_h1_r, p_h1)
gt_h2, p_h2 = align(gt_h2_r, p_h2)

docs.title: CNA Categories (Conditions)
docs.text:
The function evaluates each tool under multiple CNA “classes”, defined by conditions:

  • CN_Gain: >=2
  • CN_Neutral: =1
  • CN_Loss: =0
  • exact CN states: =2, =3, ..., =10 (folders CN_equal_2 … CN_equal_10)

Each class corresponds to a subfolder name (used in output directory structure) and a condition string (used by downstream categorization).

docs.title: Haplotype Labels
docs.text:
Haplotype naming depends on type:

  • if type="hcCNA" → hap_list = ["hap1", "hap2"]
  • if type="acCNA" → hap_list = ["minor", "major"]

These names are passed into downstream functions and appear in the final output table.

docs.title: Directory structure (per tool × CNA class)
docs.text:
For each tool and each CNA class, the function creates:

{self.output_dir}/{tool}/{folder}/

Examples:

  • .../CHISEL/CN_Gain/
  • .../CHISEL/CN_equal_3/

Inside each folder, the function writes class-specific intermediate files generated by:

  • categorize_and_save(...) (for hap1/minor and hap2/major)
  • process_folder_for_metrics_clone(...) (reads folder contents and computes metrics)

docs.title: Final aggregated CSV (outfile)
docs.text:
Saved to:

os.path.join(self.output_dir, outfile)

Default:

{self.output_dir}/cna_states.csv

docs.title: Output Table Schema
docs.text:
The returned dataframe (and saved CSV) contains one row per:

(CNA class × haplotype × clone × tool)

Columns include:

Column Meaning Type CNA class folder name (e.g., CN_Gain, CN_equal_4) Haplotype hap1/hap2 or minor/major depending on type Clone Clone identifier returned by process_folder_for_metrics_clone Tool Tool name (metrics...) Additional metric fields returned in metrics dict (depends on your implementation of process_folder_for_metrics_clone)

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text: Returns a pd.DataFrame with the aggregated per-class, per-haplotype, per-clone metrics for all tools.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from hcbench.gtbench.gtbench import GTBench

bench = GTBench(output_dir="out/gt_output", bin_size=100000 , genome="hg38")

df = bench.cna_states(
    tool_hap1_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/chisel/hap1.csv",
        "/path/to/signals/hap1.csv",
    ],
    tool_hap2_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/chisel/hap2.csv",
        "/path/to/signals/hap2.csv",
    ],
    tool_names=["CHISEL", "SIGNALS"],
    profile_hap1_cna_file="/path/to/gt/hap1.csv",
    profile_hap2_cna_file="/path/to/gt/hap2.csv",
    type="hcCNA",

    outfile="cna_states.csv",
)

print(df.head())

docs.title: Function
docs.text:
cna_values(
    self,
    tool_cna_files: List[str],
    cna_profile_file: str,
    tool_names: List[str],
    haplotype: str = "combined",

    outfile: str = "cna_values.csv",
    index_col: Optional[int] = 0,
) -> pd.DataFrame

This function evaluates bin-level CNA detection performance of multiple tools against a reference CNA profile file (ground truth).

For each tool CNA matrix, it:

  1. Loads the tool CNA file and the reference CNA file.
  2. Splits tool regions into a uniform binning resolution (self.bin_size).
  3. Aligns tool predictions and reference profiles on common regions and cells.
  4. Computes evaluation metrics (RMSE, SCC, ACC) under a specified haplotype mode.
  5. Saves a summary CSV across all tools.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description tool_cna_files List[str] List of tool CNA profile CSV files. Must align with tool_names in order. cna_profile_file str Path to the reference (truth) CNA profile CSV file. tool_names List[str] Tool names used in logs and the result table. haplotype str Haplotype evaluation mode passed to evaluate_haplotype_predictions. Default: "combined". outfile str Output filename for the summary table. Default: "cna_values.csv". index_col Optional[int] Accepted for compatibility; the method reads the named region column. Default: 0.

docs.title: cna_profile_file (truth) and each file in tool_cna_files
docs.text:
Expected to be CNA matrices with:

  • one column named region
  • remaining columns as cell IDs
  • values as CNA states (e.g., "1|1", "2|1"), consistent with your pipeline conventions

Example:

region,cell_001,cell_002,cell_003
chr1:1-100000,1|1,1|1,2|1
chr1:100001-200000,1|1,1|1,2|1

Processing:

  • Both truth and predictions are loaded with read_and_drop_empty(...) (drops empty columns/cells).
  • The truth dataframe is indexed by "region" (truth_df.set_index("region", inplace=True)).
  • Tool predictions are re-binned using:
pred = split_all_regions(pred.set_index("region"), self.bin_size)

Then truth and pred are aligned with:

truth, pred = align(truth_df, pred)

docs.title: Evaluation Metrics
docs.text:
For each tool, metrics are computed via:

rmse, scc, acc = evaluate_haplotype_predictions(pred, truth, haplotype)

The output table contains:

Column Meaning Tool Tool name RMSE Root Mean Squared Error between prediction and truth SCC Similarity/Correlation metric returned by your evaluator (often “Spearman Correlation Coefficient” in CNA contexts, but exact definition depends on your implementation) ACC Accuracy metric returned by your evaluator

Notes:

  • SCC may be None for certain inputs depending on your evaluate_haplotype_predictions implementation (e.g., constant vectors / insufficient comparable bins).

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
A single CSV is written to self.output_dir:

os.path.join(self.output_dir, outfile)

Default path:

{self.output_dir}/cna_values.csv

Example output:

Tool,RMSE,SCC,ACC
CHISEL,0.12,0.85,0.93
SIGNALS,0.20,0.71,0.88

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text:
Returns a pd.DataFrame with one row per tool and the columns:

  • Tool
  • RMSE
  • SCC
  • ACC

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from hcbench.gtbench.gtbench import GTBench

bench = GTBench(output_dir="out/gt_output", bin_size=100000 , genome="hg38")

df = bench.cna_values(
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/chisel/haplotype_combined.csv",
        "/path/to/signals/haplotype_combined.csv",
    ],
    cna_profile_file="/path/to/gt/haplotype_combined.csv",
    tool_names=["CHISEL", "SIGNALS"],
    haplotype="combined",

    outfile="cna_values.csv",
)
print(df)

docs.text:
cna_phylogeny(
    self,
    tool_cna_files: List[str],
    tool_names: List[str],
    outfile: Optional[str] = "cna_phylogeny.csv"
) -> pd.DataFrame

This function evaluates phylogenetic parsimony scores for inferred CNA profiles using the external tool LAZAC.

For each tool:

  1. Converts the CNA matrix into LAZAC-compatible input format.
  2. Runs LAZAC with nearest-neighbor interchange (NNI) tree search.
  3. Extracts the final parsimony score from the LAZAC output.
  4. Collects scores across tools into a summary table.

The function writes a single CSV file containing the parsimony scores of all tools.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description tool_cna_files List[str] List of CNA profile CSV files from different tools. Must align with tool_names in order. tool_names List[str] Tool names used for labeling outputs and result table. outfile Optional[str] Output filename for the summary table. Default: "cna_phylogeny.csv".

docs.title: Input File Format
docs.text:
Each file in tool_cna_files is expected to be a CNA matrix:

  • rows: genomic regions
  • columns: cell IDs
  • values: CNA states (e.g., "1|1", "2|1")

Example:

region,cell_001,cell_002,cell_003
chr1:1-100000,1|1,1|1,2|1
chr1:100001-200000,1|1,1|1,2|1

Before running LAZAC:

  • The CNA matrix is converted into a LAZAC-compatible input file via create_lazac_input.
  • The converted file is saved as:
{output_dir}/lazac_{tool_name}/{tool_name}_cn_profile.csv

docs.title: External Dependency
docs.text:
This function requires:

  • lazac executable available in the system PATH.
  • The command executed is:
lazac nni <cn_profile_file> -a 2 -o <output_prefix>

Where:

  • nni performs nearest-neighbor interchange search.
  • -a 2 specifies diploid assumption.
  • -o sets output prefix.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
For each tool, a dedicated directory is created:

{self.output_dir}/lazac_{tool_name}/

LAZAC generates output files including:

  • {tool_name}_info.json (contains final parsimony score)
  • additional tree-related outputs

docs.title: Summary Table (outfile)
docs.text:
Saved to:

os.path.join(self.output_dir, outfile)

Structure:

Column Meaning Tool Tool name Parsimony Final parsimony score extracted from LAZAC output

Example:

Tool,Parsimony
CHISEL,14331085
Alleloscope,34
SIGNALS,5577962

Lower parsimony scores indicate simpler evolutionary histories under the parsimony model.

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text:
Returns a pd.DataFrame containing:

Column Meaning Tool Tool name Parsimony Parsimony score

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from hcbench.realbench.realbench import RealBench

bench = RealBench(output_dir="out/real_output", bin_size=100000 , genome="hg38")

bench.cna_phylogeny(
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/chisel/cna.csv",
        "/path/to/signals/cna.csv",
    ],
    tool_names=["CHISEL", "SIGNALS"],
    outfile="cna_phylogeny.csv"
)

docs.text:
global_cn_phasing(
    self,
    tool_hap1_cna_files: List[str],
    tool_hap2_cna_files: List[str],
    tool_names: List[str],
    ground_truth_hap1_file: str,
    ground_truth_hap2_file: str,
    outprefix="global_cn_phasing",

    mode="Shared-heterozygous",
    is_clone=False,
) -> pd.DataFrame

This function evaluates haplotype phasing accuracy of inferred haplotype-specific CNAs (hap1/hap2) against ground-truth haplotype CNAs.

It converts both GT and tool haplotype CN profiles into a binary phasing representation, then computes:

  • mismatch error (per cell or per clone)
  • switch error (per cell or per clone)

It supports evaluation at cell-level (default) or clone-level (is_clone=True), and allows different evaluation modes (e.g., Shared-heterozygous).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description tool_hap1_cna_files List[str] List of tool CNA profile CSVs for inferred haplotype 1. Must align with tool_names. tool_hap2_cna_files List[str] List of tool CNA profile CSVs for inferred haplotype 2. Must align with tool_names. tool_names List[str] Tool names used in output rows. ground_truth_hap1_file str Path to ground-truth haplotype-1 CNA matrix CSV. ground_truth_hap2_file str Path to ground-truth haplotype-2 CNA matrix CSV. outprefix str Prefix for the output CSV filename. Default: "global_cn_phasing". mode str Evaluation mode passed to mismatch/switch error functions. Default: "Shared-heterozygous". is_clone bool If True, compute errors per clone label; otherwise per cell. Default: False.

docs.title: Ground truth files (ground_truth_hap1_file, ground_truth_hap2_file)
docs.text:
Loaded via read_and_drop_empty(...) and indexed by region:

g1_r = read_and_drop_empty(ground_truth_hap1_file)
g2_r = read_and_drop_empty(ground_truth_hap2_file)
g1_r.set_index("region", inplace=True)
g2_r.set_index("region", inplace=True)

Expected structure:

  • region column
  • remaining columns: cell IDs (or clone labels if evaluating clone-level elsewhere in your pipeline)
  • values: haplotype-specific CNA states (numeric or string convertible, depending on _phase_to_binary)

docs.title: Tool prediction files (tool_hap1_cna_files, tool_hap2_cna_files)
docs.text:
Also expected to have:

  • region column
  • cell/clone columns
  • haplotype-specific CNA values

docs.title: Processing Steps
docs.text:
For each tool:

  1. Read predicted haplotype profiles:
t1 = read_and_drop_empty(f_h1)
t2 = read_and_drop_empty(f_h2)
  1. Re-bin regions to the configured bin_size:
t1 = split_all_regions(t1.set_index("region"), self.bin_size)
t2 = split_all_regions(t2.set_index("region"), self.bin_size)
  1. Align predictions with GT on common regions and samples:
g1, t1 = align(g1_r, t1)
g2, t2 = align(g2_r, t2)
  1. Convert haplotype CNAs to a binary phasing representation:
g1_bin, _ = self._phase_to_binary(g1, g2)
t1_bin, _ = self._phase_to_binary(t1, t2)

_phase_to_binary is expected to encode phasing comparisons bin-wise (e.g., indicating whether hap1 > hap2, hap1 < hap2, or equal), producing matrices suitable for mismatch/switch evaluation.

docs.title: Error Metrics
docs.text:
The function chooses evaluation routines based on is_clone:

  • if is_clone=False (default):
  • simu_cell_mismatch_error
  • simu_cell_switch_error
  • if is_clone=True:
  • simu_clone_mismatch_error
  • simu_clone_switch_error

Both mismatch and switch error functions are called with:

  • predicted binary matrix t1_bin
  • GT binary matrix g1_bin
  • mode (e.g., "Shared-heterozygous")
mismatch_error_result = eval_mismatch_fn(t1_bin, g1_bin, mode)
switch_error_result   = eval_switch_fn(t1_bin, g1_bin, mode)

The two result tables are merged on:

  • cell (cell-level), or
  • clone_label (clone-level)
label = "clone_label" if is_clone else "cell"
result = pd.merge(mismatch_error_result, switch_error_result, on=label, how="outer")
result["tool_name"] = name

docs.text:
A single CSV is written to self.output_dir:

os.path.join(self.output_dir, f"{outprefix}_{mode}.csv")

Default example:

{self.output_dir}/global_cn_phasing_Shared-heterozygous.csv

The output is long-format, with one row per cell/clone (depending on is_clone) per tool.

docs.text:
Exact columns depend on what your mismatch/switch routines return, but typically include:

Column Meaning cell or clone_label Identifier used for per-sample evaluation mismatch-related columns e.g., mismatch count / mismatch ratio switch-related columns e.g., switch error count / switch error ratio tool_name Tool name

  3. Produces predicted CN-change labels/values (Change_predict) and compares them to GT Change.

h1 = self._onset_join(change_truth, p_h1, "hap1")

comb = pd.concat([h1, h2], ignore_index=True)

rmse = self._cn_change_rmse(gt, pd_)
acc  = self._cn_change_acc(gt, pd_)

Column Meaning Tool Tool name Type Change category label from the GT table RMSE CN-change RMSE computed by self._cn_change_rmse ACC CN-change accuracy computed by self._cn_change_acc

  • The exact interpretation of RMSE and ACC depends on how Change / Change_predict are encoded and how _cn_change_rmse / _cn_change_acc are implemented (numeric vs categorical).

This function evaluates copy-number stability accuracy along a given phylogenetic tree.

Given:

  • a tree (Newick format),
  • a segment change table (changes_file),
  • and each tool’s haplotype-specific CNA profiles (hap1/hap2),

it builds a set of “stability checks” derived from the tree topology and then measures, for each tool, how often predicted CN states satisfy the expected stability constraints. Results are reported as ACC (mean of boolean check outcomes), stratified by change Type.

docs.text: Name Type Description tool_hap1_cna_files List[str] List of tool CNA profile CSVs for haplotype 1. Must align with tool_names. tool_hap2_cna_files List[str] List of tool CNA profile CSVs for haplotype 2. Must align with tool_names. tool_names List[str] Tool names used in result rows. changes_file str Path to the segment/change table used for stability checks (must include Segment, Type, and other fields used by internal helpers). tree_file str Path to the phylogenetic tree file in Newick format. outfile str Output filename for the summary table. Default: "complex_hccna_stability.csv".

docs.title: tree_file (Newick tree)
docs.text:
Read using Biopython:

tree = Phylo.read(tree_file, "newick")

So the tree must be a valid Newick string/file (tip names must match whatever identifiers your stability logic expects).

docs.title: changes_file (segment/change table)
docs.text:
Loaded via:

change_df = read_and_drop_empty(changes_file)

Expected to contain at least:

  • Segment: genomic interval key used for binning and joining
  • Type: category label used for stratified reporting

Optional:

  • Haplotype: if present, will be normalized via self._normalize_hap_label(...)

Preprocessing steps:

  1. Add a checklist derived from the tree:
change_df = self._add_check_list(tree, change_df)
  1. Re-bin segments:
change_df = split_all_regions(change_df.set_index("Segment"), self.bin_size)
change_df = change_df.reset_index().rename(columns={"index": "Segment"})
  1. Normalize haplotype labels if provided.

docs.title: Tool CNA Profile Format
docs.text:
Each file in tool_hap1_cna_files / tool_hap2_cna_files is expected to be a CNA matrix with:

  • region column
  • remaining columns as cell IDs
  • values: haplotype-specific CN states

They are loaded and re-binned:

p_h1 = split_all_regions(p_h1.set_index("region"), self.bin_size).reset_index()
p_h2 = split_all_regions(p_h2.set_index("region"), self.bin_size).reset_index()

docs.title: Evaluation Logic
docs.text:
For each tool:

  1. Copy the processed change table:
proc = change_df.copy()
  1. Populate row-wise stability check outcomes using predictions:
self._process_change_rows(proc, p_h1, p_h2)

This helper is expected to add/overwrite a column:

  • result: a per-row boolean or numeric indicator (e.g., 1.0/0.0) showing whether the stability condition is satisfied for that row.

  • Aggregate accuracy per Type:

acc = proc[proc["Type"] == t]["result"].mean()

  1. Append one summary row per (Tool × Type):

  2. Tool

  3. Type
  4. ACC (mean stability satisfaction rate)

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
A single CSV summary is written to self.output_dir:

os.path.join(self.output_dir, outfile)

Default:

{self.output_dir}/complex_hccna_stability.csv

docs.title: Output Table Schema
docs.text:
One row per (Tool × Type):

Column Meaning Tool Tool name Type Change/stability category from changes_file ACC Mean of result for that type (stability accuracy rate)

Notes:

  • If result is boolean, pandas will treat True/False as 1/0 when computing .mean().
  • If a Type has no rows, it will not appear in the output (because types are taken from proc['Type'].unique()).

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text:
Returns a pd.DataFrame with columns:

  • Tool
  • Type
  • ACC

This function evaluates tool performance on Mirrored-Subclonal CNA (MSCNA) events by comparing predicted haplotype CNAs for two paired clones against a ground-truth MSCNA table.

Given:

  • a ground-truth MSCNA event table (changes_file) describing two related subclones (Clone1/Clone2) and their haplotype CN states,
  • and each tool’s inferred CNA matrix,

it:

  1. Converts MSCNA event intervals into a region key and re-bins to the configured bin_size.
  2. Re-bins tool predictions to the same resolution.
  3. Merges GT MSCNA events with tool predictions using _mirror_merge.
  4. Computes:
  5. ACC: fraction of events where all four haplotype CN states (Clone1 hap1/hap2 + Clone2 hap1/hap2) match exactly.
  6. RMSE: mean per-event haplotype error aggregated across the four haplotype states.

Results are summarized per tool and written to disk.

change_df_r = read_and_drop_empty(changes_file)

  • Chromosome
  • Start
  • End

These are combined into a genomic interval string:

change_df_r["region"] = f"{Chromosome}:{Start}-{End}"

The event table also needs the paired clone identifiers and GT CNA fields used in the comparison. The merged result contains:

  • Clone1_CNA, Clone2_CNA (GT haplotype CNA encoded as "hap1|hap2")
  • Clone1_predict_CNA, Clone2_predict_CNA (predicted haplotype CNA encoded as "hap1|hap2")

GT events are re-binned:

change_truth_r = split_all_regions(change_df_r.set_index("region"), self.bin_size)
change_truth_r = change_truth_r.reset_index().rename(columns={"index": "region"})

docs.title: Tool CNA files (tool_cna_files)
docs.text:
Expected to be CNA matrices with:

  • region column
  • cell/clone columns depending on your pipeline
  • CNA values encoded as haplotype strings like "a|b" (required for hap split)

Tool predictions are re-binned similarly:

pred = split_all_regions(pred.set_index("region"), self.bin_size).reset_index()

docs.title: Processing Steps
docs.text:
For each tool:

  1. Merge GT MSCNA table with predictions:
combined = self._mirror_merge(change_df, pred)

If combined is empty, RMSE and ACC are set to NaN.

  1. Split haplotype CNA strings for both clones:

For each side in ["Clone1", "Clone2"], the function derives:

  • {side}_hap1_CNA, {side}_hap2_CNA (GT)
  • {side}_predict_hap1_CNA, {side}_predict_hap2_CNA (prediction)

by splitting "hap1|hap2".

docs.title: 1) ACC (Exact match accuracy)
docs.text:
An event is counted as correct only if all four haplotype values match exactly:

  • Clone1 hap1 and hap2
  • Clone2 hap1 and hap2
acc = mean(
    Clone1_pred_h1 == Clone1_gt_h1 AND
    Clone1_pred_h2 == Clone1_gt_h2 AND
    Clone2_pred_h1 == Clone2_gt_h1 AND
    Clone2_pred_h2 == Clone2_gt_h2
)

So ACC is the fraction of MSCNA events fully matched across both clones and both haplotypes.

docs.title: 2) RMSE (Aggregated per-event haplotype error)
docs.text:
Per haplotype value, squared error is computed after coercing to numeric:

se = (pred - gt)^2

Then per-event RMSE-like aggregate is computed as:

RMSE_result =
    sqrt(Clone1_hap1_error) +
    sqrt(Clone1_hap2_error) +
    sqrt(Clone2_hap1_error) +
    sqrt(Clone2_hap2_error)

Finally, the reported RMSE is the mean of RMSE_result across events.

Note: This is not a conventional single RMSE over all values; it is a sum of per-haplotype absolute errors (since sqrt((a-b)^2) = |a-b|) averaged across events.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
A single CSV summary is written to self.output_dir:

os.path.join(self.output_dir, outfile)

Default:

{self.output_dir}/mirrored_subclonal_cnas_cnas.csv

docs.title: Output Table Schema
docs.text:
One row per tool:

Column Meaning Tool Tool name RMSE Mean aggregated haplotype absolute error across Clone1/Clone2 (as defined above) ACC Exact-match accuracy requiring all four haplotype values to match

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text:
Returns a pd.DataFrame with columns:

  • Tool
  • RMSE
  • ACC

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from hcbench.gtbench import GTBench

bench = GTBench(output_dir="out/gt_output", bin_size=100000 , genome="hg38")

df = bench.mirrored_subclonal_cnas(
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/chisel/haplotype_combined.csv",
        "/path/to/signals/haplotype_combined.csv",
    ],
    tool_names=["CHISEL", "SIGNALS"],
    changes_file="/path/to/gt/mirrored_subclone_events.csv",

    outfile="mirrored_subclonal_cnas.csv",
)

print(df)

docs.title: 1. cna_values
docs.text:
Calculates RMSE, ACC, and SCC for evaluating CN detection at the bin level. It compares predicted CN profiles from different tools to the ground truth.

Output: cna_values.csv

docs.title: 2. cna_states
docs.text:
Evaluates the accuracy of CN state classification across bins. Supports both acCNA and hcCNA modes and computes AUROC, AUPRC, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score for each tool.

Output: Categorized CNV CSV files and evaluation summary tables.

docs.title: 3. cn_change_at_onset
docs.text:
Determines whether CN changes between parent and child clones are correctly identified. Evaluates the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Accuracy (ACC) for each tool.

Output: cn_change_at_onset.csv

docs.title: 4. complex_hccna_stability
docs.text:
Computes Evolutionary CN Stability based on phylogenetic tree relationships between clones. Requires both maternal/paternal CNA files and a tree.newick file describing clone hierarchy.

Output: complex_hccna_stability.csv

docs.title: 5. hconsetccc
docs.text:
Determines whether CN events are correctly detected at their first evolutionary branch. This submodule evaluates accuracy (ACC) across DEL/DUP events.

Output: complex_hccna_at_onset.csv

docs.title: 6. parental_cn_at_onset
docs.text:
Assesses whether parental CN states are correctly inferred during evolution. Evaluates both RMSE and ACC.

Output: parental_cn_at_onset.csv

docs.title: 7. hcphasing
docs.text:
Quantifies haplotype phasing accuracy using two metrics:

  • Mismatch Error: Fraction of individual loci where predicted haplotypes differ from the ground truth.
  • Switch Error: Frequency of phase switches between consecutive loci.

Output: global_cn_phasing.csv

docs.title: 8. mirrored_subclonal_cnas
docs.text:
Evaluates accuracy of detecting mirror-subclone CNAs, using RMSE and ACC. Mirror-subclones are pairs of subclones that exhibit complementary CNA patterns.

Output: mirrored_subclonal_cnas_cnas.csv

docs.title: 9. subdetect
docs.text:
Calculates Adjusted Mutual Information (AMI) and Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) to measure clustering accuracy of predicted clone structures. Each classification file should contain cell_id and clone_id columns.

Output: AMI_ARI_results.csv

docs.title: Function
docs.text:
complex_hccnas(
    self,
    gt_cna_file: str,
    tool_cna_files: List[str],
    tool_names: List[str],

    threshold=0.8,
    outprefix: str = "complex_hccnas_",
    level="cell",
    changes_file: Optional[str] = ""
)

This function evaluates complex_hccnas quality of CNA calls by comparing tool predictions against GT-derived CNA segments.

It first derives CNA segments from the ground-truth CNA matrix using annotate_segments(...) (with optional CNV type detection). Then, for each tool, it converts the tool CNA matrix into a long format (region × cell), re-bins regions to a uniform resolution, and computes complex_hccnas metrics using get_segment_metric(...).

A single metrics CSV is written to disk.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Name Type Description gt_cna_file str Path to GT CNA matrix CSV (regions × cells). The first column is treated as index when reading. tool_cna_files List[str] List of tool CNA profile CSVs. Must align with tool_names. tool_names List[str] Tool names used to label metric outputs. threshold float Threshold passed into annotate_segments(...) (used for complex_hccnas/CNV detection sensitivity). Default: 0.8. outprefix str Prefix used for the output metrics filename. Default: "complex_hccnas_". level str Placeholder for evaluation level ("cell" or "clone"). Currently only "cell" path is active. changes_file Optional[str] Optional change-table path accepted by the method; default: "".

docs.title: gt_cna_file (GT CNA matrix)
docs.text:
Loaded as:

gt_profile = pd.read_csv(gt_cna_file, index_col=0)

So the CSV is expected to be:

  • rows: genomic regions (in the index)
  • columns: cell IDs
  • values: CNA states

Example:

region,cell_001,cell_002
chr1:1-100000,1|1,1|1
chr1:100001-200000,2|1,2|1

The GT matrix is transposed before complex_hccnas annotation:

gt_annotated_df = annotate_segments(gt_profile.T, detect_cnv_type=True, threshold=threshold)

annotate_segments(...) is expected to return a dataframe that includes (at minimum):

  • Chrom
  • Start
  • End

A region string is then constructed:

gt_annotated_df["region"] = (
    gt_annotated_df["Chrom"] + ":" +
    gt_annotated_df["Start"].astype(str) + "-" +
    gt_annotated_df["End"].astype(str)
)

docs.title: Tool CNA files (tool_cna_files)
docs.text:
Loaded via:

tool_cna_df = read_and_drop_empty(f)

Expected to include a region column plus one column per cell (wide CNA matrix).

Example:

region,cell_001,cell_002
chr1:1-100000,1|1,1|1
chr1:100001-200000,2|1,2|1

docs.title: Processing Steps
docs.text:
For each tool:

  1. Convert wide CNA matrix to long format (one row per region × cell):
tool_cna_df_long = (
    pd.DataFrame(tool_cna_df)
      .melt(id_vars="region", var_name="cell", value_name="value")
      .dropna(subset=["value"])
)
  1. Re-bin/split regions to the configured bin_size resolution:
tool_cna_df_long = split_all_regions(tool_cna_df_long.set_index("region"), self.bin_size)
tool_cna_df_long = tool_cna_df_long.reset_index().rename(columns={"index": "region"})
  1. Compute complex_hccnas metrics comparing tool calls to GT segments:
result2 = get_segment_metric(gt_annotated_df, tool_cna_df_long)
result2["Tool"] = name
  1. Collect per-tool metric outputs and concatenate:
metric_df = pd.concat(metric_results, ignore_index=True)

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
A single CSV is written to self.output_dir:

os.path.join(self.output_dir, f"{outprefix}metrics.csv")

Default:

{self.output_dir}/segmentation_metrics.csv

The output rows depend on what get_segment_metric(...) returns (e.g., overlap scores, breakpoint precision/recall, CNV-type metrics, etc.), with an added column:

  • Tool

docs.title: Return Value
docs.text: This function does not explicitly return a value (runtime return is None).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from hcbench.gtbench.gtbench import GTBench

bench = GTBench(output_dir="out/gt_output", bin_size=100000 , genome="hg38")

bench.complex_hccnas(
    gt_cna_file="/path/to/gt/haplotype_combined.csv",
    tool_cna_files=[
        "/path/to/chisel/haplotype_combined.csv",
        "/path/to/signals/haplotype_combined.csv",
    ],
    tool_names=["CHISEL", "SIGNALS"],

    threshold=0.8,
    outprefix="complex_hccnas_",
)

docs.title: HCBench Parsers
docs.text: Use a parser to convert a caller's output into region-by-cell CNA matrices before benchmarking.

docs.title: Prepare caller output
docs.text:
Parser Main Input Additional Inputs Format Types Supported Outputs CHISEL calls.tsv mapping.tsv, VAF table Tab-delimited text CNA Matrix, Clusters, Bin Counts, Sparse VAF Alleloscope .rds files clusters.csv, raw counts TSV, cellSNP directory R serialized data, TSV, CSV CNA Matrix, Clusters, Bin Counts, Sparse VAF CNRein CNReinPrediction.csv .npz arrays, split VCF files CSV, NPZ, VCF CNA Matrix, Bin RDR, Sparse VAF SEACON calls.tsv counts.tsv, vaf.tsv Tab-delimited text Split CNA Matrices, Bin Counts, Sparse VAF SIGNALS hscn.rds (exported to .tsv) cluster file, bin counts, VAF table Tab-delimited text / CSV CNA Matrix, Clusters, Bin Counts, Sparse VAF HCDSIM GT cell_cna_profile.csv — CSV CNA matrices, event annotation, event counts

Choose the caller page above for its required columns and optional inputs. Create the output directory before parsing. Cluster, read-depth, and VAF files are generated by separate methods when the corresponding inputs are available.

docs.title: Initialize and parse
docs.text:
bin_size and genome are required when creating a CNA parser, GTBench, or RealBench:

  • bin_size: a positive integer in base pairs, such as 100000 for 100 kb. It sets the event-analysis resolution and, when expand_bins=True, the maximum length of each output region.
  • genome: "hg19" or "hg38", matching your input coordinates.

expand_bins=False is the default. Passing bin_size alone does not split CNA regions; initialization prints Expand bins: False (regions will not be split). Set expand_bins=True to split each input region into pieces no longer than bin_size before the CNA matrices are written. Initialization then prints Expand bins: True (regions will be split). The split pieces keep the input region's CNA values. bin_size is still used for event-analysis resolution when splitting is off.

Methods use this configuration. Initialization prints:

Bin size: 100000 bp
Genome: hg38
Expand bins: True (regions will be split)

This example reads a CHISEL table containing #CHR, START, END, CELL, and HAP_CN:

from pathlib import Path
from hcbench.parsers.chisel import ChiselParser

output = Path("results/CHISEL")
output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
parser = ChiselParser(
    input_path="chisel/calls/calls.tsv",
    output_path=str(output),
    bin_size=100000,
    genome="hg38",
    expand_bins=True,
)
parser.run()

With expand_bins=True, the parser splits each input region into pieces of at most 100,000 bp before writing the matrices. run() writes haplotype_combined.csv, haplotype_1.csv, haplotype_2.csv, minor.csv, major.csv, and minor_major.csv for this example. Each CSV has a region column and one column per cell. SEACON writes only minor/major matrices by default; use output_haplotype=True for haplotype outputs. CHISEL can write separate clone and cell subdirectories when two value_cols are specified; see its caller page.

docs.title: Annotate CNA events
docs.text:
After parsing, annotate the combined profile when you need event sizes and types:

annotated = parser.annotate_segments(
    "results/CHISEL/haplotype_combined.csv",
    out_file="annotated_segments.csv",
    threshold=0.8,
    detect_cnv_type=True
)

This writes results/CHISEL/annotated_segments.csv and returns the annotation DataFrame. Rows include cell, Chrom, Start, End, value, Segment, size, and type. The annotation defaults are threshold=0.8 and detect_cnv_type=True. Use chromosomes=["chr1", "chr2"] to select chromosomes; separate chromosome CSVs are also saved. With no selection, all input chromosomes are included.

With the default event-size thresholds, analysis is available for:

CNA bin_size Event categories <= 3,000,000 bp focal, medium, broad > 3,000,000 and <= 10,000,000 bp medium, broad > 10,000,000 bp broad

Event length is End - Start + 1: focal is below 3 Mb, medium is from 3 Mb through 10 Mb, and broad is above 10 Mb. Whole-chromosome and whole-genome events are reported as broad. Categories unavailable at your resolution have no annotation or category-metric rows; a missing comparison is reported as NA rather than evidence of no events.

For this method, small_size (default 3_000_000) and mid_size (default 10_000_000) set the event-size thresholds and corresponding resolution limits.

docs.title: Annotate ground truth
docs.text:
For HCDSIM ground truth, prepare a CSV with chromosome coordinates and one column per cell. See HCDSIM GT for parsing, event annotation, event counts, and input requirements.

Use the standardized matrices with GTBench when ground truth is available, or RealBench to compare callers.

docs.title: Alleloscope Parser
docs.text:
This module provides AlleloscopeParser, specialized for parsing Alleloscope outputs and exporting standardized matrices and helper files used by hcbench workflows.

Key features:

  • Read Alleloscope RDS outputs (genotypes and segmentation table) and convert them into a unified haplotype level CNA matrix
  • Optional region splitting with expand_bins=True and the required bin_size
  • Parse Alleloscope cluster assignments into a standardized clusters.csv
  • Export bin-level count matrices as bin_counts.csv
  • Convert a cellSNP-like VAF long table into sparse matrix outputs

bin_size (positive integer, bp) and genome ("hg19" or "hg38") are required. Creating the parser prints both values. expand_bins=False leaves input CNA regions intact and prints that they will not be split. Set expand_bins=True to split each input region into pieces of at most bin_size bp before writing CNA matrices; the parser prints that splitting is enabled. The pieces keep the input CNA values. bin_size also controls event-analysis resolution when splitting is off. Install the rds extra to read RDS inputs.

docs.title: 🧬 1. Parse the CNA Matrix from RDS
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from hcbench.parsers.alleloscope import AlleloscopeParser

Path("output/alleloscope").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

allelo_output = "output/alleloscope/"
genotypes_rds = "/demo_output/alleloscope/output/rds/genotypes.rds"
seg_table_rds = "/demo_output/alleloscope/output/rds/seg_table.rds"

alleloscope_parser = AlleloscopeParser(
    output_path=allelo_output,
    genotypes_rds_path=genotypes_rds,
    seg_table_rds_path=seg_table_rds,
    barcode_path=None,
    bin_size=100000,
    start_offset=1,         # shift start coordinate by +1 if needed
    genome="hg38",
)

alleloscope_parser.run()

After running, the parser will read the two RDS files and save results to the output directory, typically containing files, for example:

output/alleloscope/
  haplotype_combined.csv
  haplotype_1.csv
  haplotype_2.csv
  minor.csv
  major.csv
  minor_major.csv

docs.title: 🧬 2. Parse the Cluster File
docs.text:
cluster_file = "/demo_output/alleloscope/output/clusters.csv"
alleloscope_parser.get_cluster(cluster_file)

After running this command, the following standardized file will be created:

output/alleloscope/
  clusters.csv

with content:

cell_id,clone_id
cellA,1
cellB,1
cellC,2

docs.title: 🧬 3. Parse the bin counts matrix
docs.text:
counts_file = "/demo_output/alleloscope/input/counts/raw_counts.tsv"
alleloscope_parser.get_bin_counts(counts_file)

After running this command, the following standardized file will be created:

output/alleloscope/
  bin_counts.csv

docs.title: 🧬 4. Parse the VAF sparse matrices
docs.text:
This method assumes vaf_file_path is a directory containing cellSNP style outputs such as:

  • cellSNP.samples.tsv
  • cellSNP.tag.AD.mtx
  • cellSNP.tag.DP.mtx
  • cellSNP.base.vcf.gz
alleloscope_parser.get_VAF_matrix(
    vaf_file_path="/demo_output/alleloscope/cellSNP_out",
    min_dp=3,
    min_cells=10,
    prefix="cellSNP",
)

Output:

output/alleloscope/
  VAF/
    cellSNP.VAF.filtered.mtx
    ...

docs.title: ⚙️ Initialization
docs.text:
AlleloscopeParser(
    output_path: str,
    genotypes_rds_path: str,
    seg_table_rds_path: str,
    *, bin_size: int, genome: str,
    expand_bins: bool = False,
    barcode_path: str | None = None,
    add_chr_prefix: bool = True,
    start_offset: int = 1,
)

output_path : base output directory.

genotypes_rds_path : Path to the Alleloscope genotypes RDS file.

seg_table_rds_path: Path to the Alleloscope segmentation table RDS file. It is used to map region identifiers into standardized region labels like:

  • chr<CHR>:<START+start_offset>-<END> when add_chr_prefix=True
  • <CHR>:<START+start_offset>-<END> when add_chr_prefix=False

barcode_path (optional) :Path to a barcode mapping file used to remap cell IDs

bin_size (required): Positive integer CNA resolution in base pairs.

add_chr_prefix (default True) :Controls whether to prepend "chr" when forming the region label from the segmentation table.

start_offset (default 1) :Adds an offset to the start coordinate when forming region labels.

docs.title: AlleloscopeParser.run()
docs.text:
Executes the standard pipeline for the CNA matrix:

  • Reads the provided genotypes_rds_path and seg_table_rds_path.
  • Standardizes genomic regions based on start_offset and add_chr_prefix.
  • Splits regions up to the initialization bin_size when expand_bins=True.
  • Writes the unified haplotype matrices directly into output_path.

docs.title: AlleloscopeParser.get_cluster(cluster_file_path)
docs.text:
Parses an Alleloscope cluster mapping file and writes a standardized CSV.

Input

  • cluster_file_path: CSV file containing at least the cell identifiers and their corresponding cluster/clone IDs.

Output writes to:

  • {self.output_path}/clusters.csv, ensuring cell_id and clone_id column formatting.

docs.title: AlleloscopeParser.get_bin_counts(counts_file)
docs.text:
Creates a region-by-cell wide matrix of per-bin counts.

Input

  • counts_file: Path to the raw bin counts TSV file.

Output writes to:

  • {self.output_path}/bin_counts.csv

This is a wide matrix:

  • rows: region
  • columns: cells
  • values: counts

docs.title: AlleloscopeParser.get_VAF_matrix(vaf_file_path, output_path=None, min_dp=1, min_cells=1, prefix="cellSNP")
docs.text:
Converts cellSNP-like VAF outputs into sparse matrix outputs.

Input format

vaf_file_path must be a directory containing cellSNP-style outputs such as:

  • cellSNP.samples.tsv
  • cellSNP.tag.AD.mtx
  • cellSNP.tag.DP.mtx
  • cellSNP.base.vcf.gz

Parameters

output_path (optional)

  • If provided: outputs under {output_path}/VAF, else outputs under {self.output_path}/VAF.
min_dp
  • Filter low depth sites.
min_cells
  • Filter sites supported by too few cells.
prefix
  • Output file prefix (default: cellSNP).

Output

Creates a VAF/ directory containing the sparse matrix (.mtx) files.

docs.title: 🧬 Generating a Cluster File in R
docs.text:
If you wish to generate the Alleloscope clustering file from your processed object in R, you can use the following commands:

linplot = Lineage_plot(Obj_filtered = Obj_filtered, nSNP = 2000, nclust = 10)
write.csv(linplot, file = "cluster.csv", row.names = TRUE)

This will create a cluster.csv file that can be used as input to AlleloscopeParser.get_cluster() in Python.

docs.title: CHISEL Parser
docs.text:
This module provides ChiselParser, specialized for parsing CHISEL outputs and exporting standardized matrices and helper files used by hcbench workflows.

Key features:

  • Run the parsing pipeline on CHISEL CNA tables
  • Optional two-pass execution to export two different value columns into: clone_level/,cell_level/
  • Parse CHISEL cluster assignments into a standardized clusters.csv
  • Export bin-level count matrices as bin_counts.csv
  • Convert a cellSNP-like VAF long table into sparse matrix outputs

bin_size (positive integer, bp) and genome ("hg19" or "hg38") are required. Creating the parser prints both values. expand_bins=False leaves input CNA regions intact and prints that they will not be split. Set expand_bins=True to split each input region into pieces of at most bin_size bp before writing CNA matrices; the parser prints that splitting is enabled. The pieces keep the input CNA values. bin_size also controls event-analysis resolution when splitting is off.

docs.title: 🧬  1. Parse the CNA Matrix

from pathlib import Path
from hcbench.parsers.chisel import ChiselParser

chisel_parser.get_bin_counts()

output/chisel/
└──bin_counts.csv

docs.text:
chisel_parser.get_VAF_matrix(
    vaf_file_path="/demo_output/chisel/baf/baf.tsv",
    min_dp=3,
    min_cells=10,
)

After running this command, the following standardized file will be created:

output/chisel/
├── VAF/
│   └──cellSNP_*.mtx

docs.title: ⚙️ Initialization
docs.text:
ChiselParser(
    input_path: str,
    output_path: str,
    *, bin_size: int, genome: str,
    expand_bins: bool = False,
    barcode_path: str | None = None,

docs.title: CNRein Parser
docs.text:
This module provides CNReinParser, specialized for parsing CNRein outputs and exporting standardized matrices and helper files used by hcbench workflows.

Key features:

  • Read CNRein prediction tables and merge separate haplotype columns into a unified haplotype-level CNA matrix
  • Optional region splitting with expand_bins=True and the required bin_size
  • Extract bin-level Read Depth Ratio (RDR) from .npz files into a standardized bin_rdr.csv
  • Convert a directory of separate chromosome VCF files into sparse VAF matrix outputs

bin_size (positive integer, bp) and genome ("hg19" or "hg38") are required. Creating the parser prints both values. expand_bins=False leaves input CNA regions intact and prints that they will not be split. Set expand_bins=True to split each input region into pieces of at most bin_size bp before writing CNA matrices; the parser prints that splitting is enabled. The pieces keep the input CNA values. bin_size also controls event-analysis resolution when splitting is off.

docs.title: 🧬 1. Parse the CNA Matrix
docs.text:
Python

from pathlib import Path
from hcbench.parsers.CNRein import CNReinParser

Path("output/cnrein").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

cnrein_input = "/demo_output/cnrein/finalPrediction/CNReinPrediction.csv"
cnrein_output = "output/cnrein/"

    input_path=cnrein_input,
    output_path=cnrein_output,
    bin_size=100000, genome="hg38",
)

cnrein_parser.run()

After running, the parser will read the input table, merge the Haplotype 1 and Haplotype 2 columns into a HAP_CN column, and save the standardized files to the output directory:

Plaintext

output/cnrein/
├── haplotype_combined.csv
├── haplotype_1.csv       
├── haplotype_2.csv       
├── minor.csv             
├── major.csv             
└── minor_major.csv
  • haplotype_combined.csv — main CNA matrix (regions × cells).

Each value represents the combined haplotype copy number in the form "hap1|hap2".

└── bin_rdr.csv

docs.title: HCDSIM ground truth (GT)
docs.text: Use GTParser to convert an HCDSIM ground-truth CNA profile into region-by-cell matrices, then annotate and count CNA events.

docs.title: Prepare the HCDSIM profile
docs.text:
The input is a CSV with Chromosome, Start, and End columns followed by one column per cell. Each row is a genomic region; each cell entry is a haplotype copy-number pair separated by |. For example:

Chromosome,Start,End,normal_cell1,normal_cell2
chr1,1,100000,1|1,1|1
chr1,100001,200000,1|1,1|1
chr1,200001,300000,2|1,1|1

Use chr-prefixed numeric chromosomes such as chr1; the current region sorter expects this form. Every data row should have the same number of fields as the header. Match the input coordinates to the genome you select.

docs.title: Parse the profile
docs.text:
bin_size is a required positive integer in base pairs, and genome is required as "hg19" or "hg38". Create the output directory, then run the parser:

from pathlib import Path
from hcbench.parsers.gt import GTParser

gt_file = "input/cell_cna_profile.csv"
output_dir = Path("output/gt")
output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

gt_parser = GTParser(
    input_path=gt_file,
    output_path=str(output_dir),
    bin_size=100000,
    genome="hg38",
)
result = gt_parser.run()

Initialization prints the bin size, genome, and whether regions will be split. With the default expand_bins=False, regions are not split. Set expand_bins=True in the constructor to split regions into pieces of at most bin_size bp. run() writes haplotype_combined.csv, haplotype_1.csv, haplotype_2.csv, minor.csv, major.csv, and minor_major.csv in output/gt/; result is None. The combined CSV has a region column, such as chr1:1-100000, followed by cell columns.

docs.title: Annotate CNA events
docs.text:
gt_parser.annotate_segments(
    str(output_dir / "haplotype_combined.csv"),
    detect_cnv_type=True,
    out_file="ground_truth_classified.csv",
)

This writes output/gt/ground_truth_classified.csv and returns None. With detect_cnv_type=True, the CSV includes cell, Chrom, Start, End, value, Segment, size, and type. The default annotation threshold is 0.8. If you omit detect_cnv_type=True, the default is False and the output has no type column. Use chromosomes=["chr1", "chr2"] to annotate selected chromosomes; the parser also writes a CSV for each selected chromosome.

With the default size thresholds, focal events are shorter than 3 Mb, medium events are 3–10 Mb, and broad events are longer than 10 Mb. The configured bin_size limits which categories are analyzed:

bin_size Categories included Up to 3 Mb focal, medium, broad Above 3 Mb and up to 10 Mb medium, broad Above 10 Mb broad

Categories outside that range are omitted from the annotation, rather than shown with a count of zero. You can set small_size and mid_size on annotate_segments() if your analysis needs different size thresholds.
